hypotheses.statement: The checkout API 5xx spike was caused by the payments-gateway.internal certificate expiring at 09:11:40Z, not by the release deployed at 09:09:52Z
The recovery at 09:57:55Z was due to certificate rotation taking effect at 09:57:50Z, not due to the rollback completed at 10:04:18Z
The release timing (two minutes before the incident) contributed to initial misdiagnosis and delayed correct root cause identification

observed_facts.statement: The release 2026.5.14-a deployed at 09:09:52Z contained copy edits to email templates and a CSV export library dependency bump
No code path in release 2026.5.14-a is reachable from POST /v2/checkout/submit
payments connector experienced TLS handshake failures due to certificate verify failed: certificate has expired
POST /v2/checkout/submit returned 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted 3 retries
The 5xx ratio returned to baseline at 09:58:10Z, six minutes before the rollback completed
The incident ticket resolution note reads only 'rolled back and recovered' and does not mention certificate rotation

open_questions.missing_evidence: Explanation for discrepancy between chat evidence and ticket resolution
open_questions.question: Why does the incident ticket resolution note not mention the certificate rotation as the root cause?

summary: Checkout API experienced a 5xx spike from 09:12:03Z to 09:58:10Z due to payments-gateway.internal certificate expiry at 09:11:40Z, causing TLS handshake failures in the payments connector. Recovery occurred after certificate rotation at 09:57:50Z, not from the subsequent rollback. Initial misdiagnosis attributed the incident to a coincidental release.
